p: Honeybees communicate through a series of movements known as the waggle dance. ______ a bee that has found food performs a dance that shows other bees the direction and distance of the source.
x: The second sentence gives a specific instance of the dance communication described in the first.
t: There’s no contrast between the sentences, which rules out the other three.

p: Many people assume that tomatoes originated in Italy, where they are central to the cuisine. ______ tomatoes are native to western South America and did not reach Europe until the 1500s.
x: The second sentence corrects the assumption in the first. “In fact” introduces the truth after a mistaken belief.
t: “As a result” would mean the assumption caused tomatoes to be South American, which makes no sense.

p: The city’s new bike lanes were separated from car traffic by concrete barriers. ______ the number of cyclists using the route doubled within a year.
x: Safer lanes led to more cyclists. That’s cause and effect.
t: “Nonetheless” signals a surprise despite something, but more riders is the expected result.

p: Early telephones required operators to connect calls by plugging cables into a switchboard. ______ automatic switching systems let callers dial numbers directly, making operators unnecessary for most calls.
x: The sentences move forward in time from manual switchboards to automatic switching.
t: Operators didn’t cause automatic switching, so “Therefore” doesn’t fit.

p: The drought cut the region’s wheat harvest by nearly 40 percent. ______ bread prices in local markets stayed stable, because the government released grain from its reserves.
x: You’d expect prices to jump after a bad harvest. They didn’t, so the second sentence is a surprise despite the first.
t: “As a result” would say the drought caused stable prices. The reserves did that.

p: Octopuses can change the color of their skin in a fraction of a second. ______ they can change its texture, raising small bumps to mimic rocks or coral.
x: Texture change is an additional ability on top of color change.
t: Texture change isn’t an example of color change, so “For example” doesn’t work.

p: Some critics dismissed the author’s first novel as overly sentimental. ______ it sold more copies in its first year than any of her later books.
x: Despite the criticism, it sold very well. “Even so” marks that concession.
t: “Therefore” would mean the criticism caused the sales.

p: Rain forests cover only about 6 percent of Earth’s land surface. ______ they are home to more than half of the world’s plant and animal species.
x: Small area, huge share of species: the second sentence contrasts with the “only” in the first.
t: “For this reason” would say their small size causes their diversity.

p: A single dairy cow can produce more than 20 liters of milk a day. ______ a herd of 200 cows can produce over 4,000 liters daily, enough to supply a small town.
x: The second sentence follows logically from the first (200 × 20 = 4,000).
t: There’s no contrast, so “However” and “In contrast” don’t work.

p: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level. ______ Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller when measured from its base on the ocean floor.
x: The second sentence qualifies the first. By another measure, a different mountain wins.
t: “Furthermore” adds a similar point, but this sentence pushes back.

p: The museum’s new exhibit focuses on everyday objects from ancient Rome. ______ rather than displaying famous statues or grand monuments, it presents cooking pots, children’s toys, and handwritten shopping lists.
x: The second sentence restates and clarifies “everyday objects” with specifics. “That is” signals clarification.
t: “In contrast” would set the exhibit against itself.

p: Sea turtles lay their eggs in nests dug into sandy beaches. ______ after hatching, the young turtles must make their way across the sand to the ocean, often at night.
x: Laying eggs comes first, then the hatchlings head to sea. It’s a sequence.
t: Nothing contrasts, so “However” is out.

p: Scientists once believed that only humans used tools. ______ researchers have since observed chimpanzees using sticks to fish for termites and crows bending wire into hooks.
x: The observations overturn the old belief, which is a contrast.
t: “As a result” would say the belief caused the observations.

p: Maria practiced the violin for two hours every day for three years. ______ she won first place at the regional competition.
x: After years of practice came the win. “Eventually” marks the payoff at the end of a long stretch.
t: “Nevertheless” implies the win was surprising given the practice. It wasn’t.

p: The first computers filled entire rooms and required teams of people to operate them. ______ today’s smartphones fit in a pocket and are thousands of times more powerful.
x: Room-sized versus pocket-sized: a direct contrast.
t: Smartphones aren’t an example of room-sized computers.

p: Recycling aluminum cans saves a great deal of energy. ______ making a can from recycled aluminum uses about 95 percent less energy than making one from raw ore.
x: The second sentence gives the precise figure behind “a great deal of energy.”
t: There’s no contrast, so “However” and “Instead” are out.

p: The novel’s first chapter is told from the point of view of a young girl. ______ the second chapter shifts to the perspective of her grandfather, looking back on the same events decades later.
x: Girl’s view versus grandfather’s view: a contrast.
t: “Likewise” would claim the chapters share the same perspective.

p: Venus is similar to Earth in size and mass. ______ its surface is hot enough to melt lead, making it very different from our planet.
x: Similar in size, very different in temperature. That’s a contrast.
t: “Similarly” ignores the “very different” at the end of the sentence.

p: Many desert plants have shallow, widespread roots that quickly absorb rainwater before it evaporates. ______ other desert plants, such as the mesquite tree, send roots deep underground to reach water far below the surface.
x: Shallow roots versus deep roots: two opposite strategies.
t: “For example” would make the mesquite an example of shallow roots.

p: The chef wanted to reduce food waste in her restaurant. ______ she began using vegetable scraps to make soup stock.
x: The action serves the goal. “To that end” means “in order to reach that goal.”
t: “Nevertheless” would mean she used scraps despite wanting less waste.

p: Early studies suggested that the new medication was highly effective. ______ larger trials involving thousands of patients found that its benefits were much smaller than first reported.
x: Later, larger trials contradicted the early results.
t: “Therefore” would say the early results caused the smaller benefits.

p: The town’s population grew rapidly after the railroad arrived in 1870. ______ new schools, churches, and shops were built to serve the growing number of residents.
x: More residents led to more buildings. “Accordingly” signals a fitting result.
t: “Previously” puts the building before the growth, but the text says they served the growing population.

p: The Great Wall of China is often described as a single wall. ______ it is a series of walls and fortifications built by different dynasties over many centuries.
x: The second sentence corrects a common description.
t: “As a result” would say the description caused the wall’s structure.

p: Some animals hibernate to survive the winter. Bears, ______ spend months in dens, living off fat stored during the summer and fall.
x: Bears are an example of animals that hibernate.
t: “In contrast” would mean bears don’t hibernate.

p: Critics praised the film’s stunning visual effects. ______ many also noted that its plot was confusing and its characters poorly developed.
x: Praise and criticism side by side. “At the same time” introduces the other side.
t: The confusing plot isn’t a result of the praised effects.

p: First, the students measured the height of each plant. ______ they recorded the measurements in a data table.
x: “First … Next” marks the steps of a process.
t: Nothing contrasts, and recording isn’t an example of measuring.

p: The author spent a decade researching the history of the region. ______ her book includes details that are not found in any earlier account.
x: Years of research produced new details. That’s cause and effect.
t: “Nevertheless” would mean the details appeared despite the research.

p: Penguins cannot fly. ______ they are excellent swimmers, using their flipper-like wings to move quickly through the water.
x: Can’t fly, but can swim well: a contrast.
t: Not flying doesn’t cause good swimming, so “Therefore” is wrong.

p: The company’s profits rose sharply last year. ______ nearly all of the increase came from a single product, leaving the company vulnerable if demand for that product falls.
x: Good news, then a caveat that undercuts it. That’s a contrast.
t: The reliance on one product isn’t caused by the rise in profits.

p: Some birds migrate thousands of kilometers each year. The Arctic tern, ______ travels from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back, a round trip of roughly 70,000 kilometers.
x: The Arctic tern is an example of a long-distance migrant.
t: “In contrast” would mean the tern doesn’t migrate far.
